convention.verticalAxis: Exchange rate: foreign currency per U.S. dollar
convention.verticalDirection: Higher means appreciation of the U.S. dollar
convention.coreSupply: Upward-sloping supply of U.S. dollars in the eight core graphs
convention.mankiwNcoSupply: Vertical supply equal to NCO in the two supplemental policy-transmission graphs

assets.imageAlt: U.S. dollar market with downward-sloping demand D0 and upward-sloping supply S0 intersecting at A.
assets.graphDescription: The vertical axis is foreign currency per U.S. dollar, so a higher value is a dollar appreciation. The horizontal axis is the quantity of U.S. dollars exchanged. Downward-sloping D0 and upward-sloping S0 intersect at A, quantity 100 and exchange rate 1.0.

assets.imageAlt: Dollar demand shifts right from D0 to D1 while upward-sloping supply S0 remains fixed.
assets.graphDescription: The vertical axis is foreign currency per U.S. dollar and the horizontal axis is the quantity of dollars exchanged. Demand shifts right from solid D0 to dashed D1 along unchanged upward-sloping S0. Equilibrium moves from A at quantity 100 and rate 1.0 to B at quantity 150 and rate 1.2.
assets.scenario: Increase in demand for U.S. dollars

assets.imageAlt: Upward-sloping dollar supply shifts right from S0 to S1 along demand D0.
assets.graphDescription: The vertical axis is foreign currency per U.S. dollar and the horizontal axis is the quantity of dollars exchanged. Demand D0 is unchanged while supply shifts right from solid S0 to dashed S1. Equilibrium moves from A at quantity 100 and rate 1.0 to B at quantity 150 and rate 0.8.
assets.scenario: Increase in supply of U.S. dollars

assets.imageAlt: Dollar demand and upward-sloping supply both shift right, from D0 and S0 to D1 and S1.
assets.graphDescription: The vertical axis is foreign currency per U.S. dollar and the horizontal axis is the quantity of dollars exchanged. Demand and supply both shift right. Original equilibrium A is quantity 100 and rate 1.0; final equilibrium B is quantity 200 and rate 1.0.
assets.scenario: Simultaneous increases in demand and supply

assets.imageAlt: Conceptual dollar market with downward-sloping demand D0 and upward-sloping supply S0.
assets.graphDescription: The vertical axis is foreign currency per U.S. dollar, with higher positions indicating dollar appreciation. The horizontal axis is the quantity of dollars exchanged. Downward-sloping D0 intersects upward-sloping S0. No numerical ticks or point labels are shown.

assets.imageAlt: Conceptual dollar market showing demand shifting right from D0 to D1 with supply S0 unchanged.
assets.graphDescription: The vertical axis is foreign currency per U.S. dollar and the horizontal axis is the quantity of dollars exchanged. Dashed demand D1 lies right of solid D0 while upward-sloping S0 is unchanged. The new intersection is above and right of the original intersection. No numerical ticks are shown.
assets.scenario: Conceptual increase in demand for U.S. dollars

assets.imageAlt: Conceptual dollar market showing upward-sloping supply shifting right from S0 to S1 with demand D0 unchanged.
assets.graphDescription: The vertical axis is foreign currency per U.S. dollar and the horizontal axis is the quantity of dollars exchanged. Dashed supply S1 lies right of solid S0 while demand D0 is unchanged. The new intersection is below and right of the original intersection. No numerical ticks are shown.
assets.scenario: Conceptual increase in supply of U.S. dollars

assets.imageAlt: Conceptual dollar market showing demand and upward-sloping supply both shifting right.
assets.graphDescription: The vertical axis is foreign currency per U.S. dollar and the horizontal axis is the quantity of dollars exchanged. Demand shifts right from D0 to D1 and supply shifts right from S0 to S1. The displayed shifts raise equilibrium quantity while leaving the exchange rate at the same vertical position. No numerical ticks are shown.
assets.scenario: Conceptual simultaneous increases in demand and supply

assets.imageAlt: Mankiw-model dollar market with vertical supply shifting left from S0 equals NCO0 to S1 equals NCO1 along D0 equals NX0.
assets.graphDescription: The vertical axis is foreign currency per U.S. dollar and the horizontal axis is the quantity of dollars exchanged. Downward-sloping D0 equals NX0. Vertical supply shifts left from S0 equals NCO0 at quantity 100 to S1 equals NCO1 at quantity 50. Equilibrium moves from A at rate 1.0 to B at rate 1.5.
assets.scenario: Decrease in NCO-determined supply of U.S. dollars

assets.imageAlt: Conceptual Mankiw-model dollar market with vertical supply shifting left from S0 equals NCO0 to S1 equals NCO1.
assets.graphDescription: The vertical axis is foreign currency per U.S. dollar and the horizontal axis is the quantity of dollars exchanged. Downward-sloping D0 equals NX0. Vertical supply shifts left from S0 equals NCO0 to S1 equals NCO1, so the new intersection is above and left of the original intersection. No numerical ticks or point labels are shown.
assets.scenario: Conceptual decrease in NCO-determined supply of U.S. dollars
